title: İlk iş günü
text: Last Monday was Selin's first day at her new job. She woke up at six because she did not want to be late. The office was in the city center, about forty minutes from her flat. When she arrived, a man called Okan was waiting for her at the door. He showed her the kitchen, the meeting rooms and her desk near the window. In the morning she read a lot of documents and tried to remember everybody's name. At lunch her new colleagues invited her to a small restaurant. They were friendly and asked her many questions. In the afternoon her manager explained the first project. Selin did not understand everything, but she wrote notes in her notebook. When she got home, she was tired but happy. She thought, "I am going to like this place."
textTr: Geçen pazartesi Selin'in yeni işindeki ilk günüydü. Geç kalmak istemediği için altıda kalktı. Ofis şehir merkezindeydi, dairesine yaklaşık kırk dakika uzaklıkta. Vardığında Okan adında bir adam kapıda onu bekliyordu. Ona mutfağı, toplantı odalarını ve pencerenin yanındaki masasını gösterdi. Sabah birçok belge okudu ve herkesin adını hatırlamaya çalıştı. Öğle yemeğinde yeni iş arkadaşları onu küçük bir restorana davet etti. Samimilerdi ve ona birçok soru sordular. Öğleden sonra müdürü ilk projeyi anlattı. Selin her şeyi anlamadı ama defterine not aldı. Eve geldiğinde yorgundu ama mutluydu. "Burayı seveceğim" diye düşündü.

questions.q: Why did Selin wake up at six?
options: She did not want to be late
questions.note: "She woke up at six because she did not want to be late."

questions.q: Who met her at the door?
questions.note: "A man called Okan was waiting for her at the door."

questions.q: What did she do during the morning?
questions.note: "She read a lot of documents."

questions.q: How did Selin feel at the end of the day?
questions.note: "She was tired but happy."

questions.q: What did she do when she did not understand?
questions.note: "She wrote notes in her notebook."

title: Kayıp telefon
text: Yesterday Baris lost his phone on the bus. He did not notice it until he arrived at the university. He looked in his bag three times, but the phone was not there. He remembered that he had put it on the seat next to him. Baris was worried because all his photographs were on that phone. He went to the bus office and explained the problem. The woman behind the desk took his name and telephone number and said, "Call us tomorrow morning." That evening Baris could not study. He kept thinking about the phone. The next day the office called him: a student had found the phone and brought it back. Baris was so happy that he bought a box of chocolates for the office staff.
textTr: Dün Barış telefonunu otobüste kaybetti. Üniversiteye varana kadar fark etmedi. Çantasına üç kez baktı ama telefon orada değildi. Onu yanındaki koltuğa koyduğunu hatırladı. Barış endişeliydi çünkü bütün fotoğrafları o telefondaydı. Otobüs bürosuna gidip sorunu anlattı. Masanın arkasındaki kadın adını ve telefon numarasını aldı ve "Yarın sabah bizi arayın" dedi. O akşam Barış ders çalışamadı. Sürekli telefonu düşündü. Ertesi gün büro onu aradı: bir öğrenci telefonu bulup getirmişti. Barış o kadar mutlu oldu ki büro çalışanlarına bir kutu çikolata aldı.

questions.q: Where did Baris lose his phone?
questions.note: "Baris lost his phone on the bus."

questions.q: Why was he worried?
options: His photographs were on the phone
He needed to call his family
questions.note: "All his photographs were on that phone."

questions.q: What did the woman ask for?
questions.note: "The woman took his name and telephone number."

questions.q: Who found the phone?
questions.note: "A student had found the phone."

questions.q: What did Baris do at the end?
options: He went back to the bus
He bought chocolates for the staff
questions.note: Teşekkür olarak çikolata aldı.

title: Köyden şehre
titleEn: From the Village to the City
text: Hasan grew up in a small village with about two hundred people. His family had sheep and a garden with fruit trees. There was only one school and one shop. When he was eighteen, he moved to the city to study engineering. At first everything was strange. The streets were noisy, the buildings were tall and nobody said hello in the morning. He missed the quiet nights and the smell of the garden. After two years he made good friends and started to enjoy the city. Now he works for a large company and lives in a modern flat. But every summer he goes back to the village for three weeks. He says the village is still his real home.
textTr: Hasan yaklaşık iki yüz kişilik küçük bir köyde büyüdü. Ailesinin koyunları ve meyve ağaçları olan bir bahçesi vardı. Sadece bir okul ve bir dükkân vardı. On sekiz yaşındayken mühendislik okumak için şehre taşındı. Başta her şey tuhaftı. Sokaklar gürültülüydü, binalar yüksekti ve sabahları kimse selam vermiyordu. Sessiz geceleri ve bahçenin kokusunu özledi. İki yıl sonra iyi arkadaşlar edindi ve şehri sevmeye başladı. Şimdi büyük bir şirkette çalışıyor ve modern bir dairede yaşıyor. Ama her yaz üç haftalığına köye dönüyor. Köyün hâlâ gerçek evi olduğunu söylüyor.

questions.q: How many people lived in the village?
questions.note: "A small village with about two hundred people."

questions.q: Why did Hasan move to the city?
questions.note: "He moved to the city to study engineering."

questions.q: What did he find difficult at first?
options: The city was noisy and strange
questions.note: "At first everything was strange. The streets were noisy."

questions.q: How often does he visit the village now?
questions.note: "Every summer he goes back to the village for three weeks."

questions.q: What does Hasan say about the village?
options: It is still his real home
questions.note: "He says the village is still his real home."

title: Spor salonu
text: Three months ago Pinar decided to change her habits. She was always tired and she never did any sport. A friend told her about a gym near the train station, so she went there on a Saturday morning to ask about the prices. The trainer showed her the machines and made a plan for her: three days a week, forty minutes each time. The first week was difficult and her legs hurt, but she did not stop. After a month she noticed that she slept better. After two months she could run for twenty minutes without a break. Now Pinar goes to the gym before work and she has more energy during the day. Her sister has decided to join her next month.
textTr: Üç ay önce Pınar alışkanlıklarını değiştirmeye karar verdi. Sürekli yorgundu ve hiç spor yapmıyordu. Bir arkadaşı ona tren istasyonunun yanındaki spor salonundan bahsetti, o da bir cumartesi sabahı fiyatları sormaya gitti. Antrenör ona aletleri gösterdi ve bir program yaptı: haftada üç gün, her seferinde kırk dakika. İlk hafta zordu ve bacakları ağrıdı ama bırakmadı. Bir ay sonra daha iyi uyuduğunu fark etti. İki ay sonra ara vermeden yirmi dakika koşabiliyordu. Şimdi Pınar işten önce spor salonuna gidiyor ve gün içinde daha çok enerjisi oluyor. Kız kardeşi de gelecek ay ona katılmaya karar verdi.

questions.q: Why did Pinar decide to change her habits?
questions.note: "She was always tired and she never did any sport."

questions.q: How often does she go to the gym?
questions.note: "Three days a week, forty minutes each time."

questions.q: What happened after one month?
options: She could run for twenty minutes
questions.note: "After a month she noticed that she slept better."

questions.q: When does Pinar go to the gym now?
questions.note: "Pinar goes to the gym before work."

questions.q: Who is going to join her?
questions.note: "Her sister has decided to join her next month."

title: Eski bir mektup
text: While Nil was cleaning the cupboard, she found a box of old letters. They were written by her grandmother more than fifty years ago. The paper was yellow and some words were difficult to read. In one letter her grandmother described her wedding day: the weather was terrible, the car did not start and the photographer arrived two hours late. But she wrote, "It was the happiest day of my life." Nil sat on the floor and read for two hours. She learned things about her family that nobody had told her. The next weekend she visited her grandmother and asked about the letters. They talked until midnight and looked at old photographs together.
textTr: Nil dolabı temizlerken eski mektuplarla dolu bir kutu buldu. Bunlar elli yıldan fazla süre önce büyükannesi tarafından yazılmıştı. Kâğıt sararmıştı ve bazı kelimeleri okumak zordu. Bir mektupta büyükannesi düğün gününü anlatıyordu: hava berbattı, araba çalışmadı ve fotoğrafçı iki saat geç geldi. Ama "Hayatımın en mutlu günüydü" diye yazmıştı. Nil yere oturup iki saat okudu. Ailesi hakkında kimsenin ona anlatmadığı şeyler öğrendi. Ertesi hafta sonu büyükannesini ziyaret edip mektupları sordu. Gece yarısına kadar konuştular ve birlikte eski fotoğraflara baktılar.

questions.q: Where did Nil find the letters?
questions.note: "While Nil was cleaning the cupboard, she found a box of old letters."

questions.q: Who wrote the letters?
questions.note: "They were written by her grandmother."

questions.q: What went wrong on the wedding day?
questions.note: "The car did not start and the photographer arrived two hours late."

questions.q: What did her grandmother write about that day?
options: It was the happiest day of her life
questions.note: Her şeye rağmen "hayatımın en mutlu günü" yazmış.

questions.q: What did Nil do the next weekend?
options: She showed the letters to friends
questions.note: "The next weekend she visited her grandmother."

title: Otel sorunu
text: Cem booked a hotel room in Antalya for four nights. On the website the photographs showed a large room with a view of the sea. When he arrived, the receptionist gave him a key for a room at the back of the building. The window looked at a car park and the air conditioning did not work. Cem went downstairs and explained the problem politely. The receptionist said the hotel was full and there were no other rooms. Cem showed her the photographs on his phone and asked for the manager. After twenty minutes the manager found a better room on the fourth floor. He also offered a free breakfast for the whole week. Cem was pleased, but he decided to read the reviews more carefully next time.
textTr: Cem Antalya'da dört gecelik bir otel odası ayırttı. İnternet sitesinde fotoğraflar deniz manzaralı büyük bir oda gösteriyordu. Vardığında resepsiyon görevlisi ona binanın arkasındaki bir odanın anahtarını verdi. Pencere otoparka bakıyordu ve klima çalışmıyordu. Cem aşağı inip sorunu kibarca anlattı. Görevli otelin dolu olduğunu ve başka oda olmadığını söyledi. Cem ona telefonundaki fotoğrafları gösterdi ve müdürü istedi. Yirmi dakika sonra müdür dördüncü katta daha iyi bir oda buldu. Ayrıca bütün hafta için ücretsiz kahvaltı teklif etti. Cem memnun oldu ama bir dahaki sefere yorumları daha dikkatli okumaya karar verdi.

questions.q: What was wrong with the first room?
options: It was on the fourth floor
It looked at a car park
questions.note: "The window looked at a car park and the air conditioning did not work."

questions.q: What did the receptionist say at first?
questions.note: "The hotel was full and there were no other rooms."

questions.q: What did Cem show her?
questions.note: "Cem showed her the photographs on his phone."

questions.q: What did the manager offer?
options: A better room and free breakfast
questions.note: Daha iyi bir oda ve bütün hafta ücretsiz kahvaltı.

questions.q: What will Cem do next time?
questions.note: "He decided to read the reviews more carefully next time."

title: Sokak kedisi
text: Last winter a thin gray cat started to sleep in front of Aylin's door. At first Aylin only gave it water, because she did not want a pet. But the nights were cold and the cat was always waiting there in the morning. One day she took it to a doctor for animals. The doctor said the cat was about two years old and quite healthy. Aylin bought a small bed and called the cat Duman. Now Duman sleeps inside and follows her from room to room. Aylin says she did not choose the cat; the cat chose her. Her neighbors often ask about Duman because he sits in the window and watches the street all day.
textTr: Geçen kış ince gri bir kedi Aylin'in kapısının önünde uyumaya başladı. Aylin başta sadece su verdi çünkü evcil hayvan istemiyordu. Ama geceler soğuktu ve kedi her sabah orada bekliyordu. Bir gün onu hayvan doktoruna götürdü. Doktor kedinin yaklaşık iki yaşında ve oldukça sağlıklı olduğunu söyledi. Aylin küçük bir yatak aldı ve kediye Duman adını verdi. Şimdi Duman içeride uyuyor ve odadan odaya onu takip ediyor. Aylin kediyi kendisinin seçmediğini, kedinin onu seçtiğini söylüyor. Komşuları sık sık Duman'ı soruyor çünkü bütün gün pencerede oturup sokağı izliyor.

questions.q: Where did the cat sleep at first?
questions.note: "A thin gray cat started to sleep in front of Aylin's door."

questions.q: Why did Aylin only give water at first?
options: She did not want a pet
questions.note: "She did not want a pet."

questions.q: What did the doctor say?
questions.note: "The cat was about two years old and quite healthy."

questions.q: What does Aylin say about the cat?
options: She will find a new home for it
questions.note: "She did not choose the cat; the cat chose her."

questions.q: Why do the neighbors ask about Duman?
options: He sits in the window all day
questions.note: Pencerede oturup sokağı izlediği için herkes onu görüyor.

title: Bisikletle işe
text: Tolga used to drive to work every morning. The journey was only six kilometers, but it often took him thirty minutes because of the traffic. Last spring he bought a bicycle. On the first day he was slow and arrived late, but after two weeks he was faster than his car. Now he saves money and he arrives at the office awake and in a good mood. Of course there are problems. When it rains he gets wet, and in winter it is dark when he comes home. His wife thinks the roads are dangerous, so Tolga always wears a helmet and bright clothes. He says he will never go back to driving.
textTr: Tolga eskiden her sabah işe arabayla giderdi. Yol sadece altı kilometreydi ama trafik yüzünden çoğu zaman otuz dakika sürüyordu. Geçen ilkbahar bir bisiklet aldı. İlk gün yavaştı ve geç kaldı ama iki hafta sonra arabasından daha hızlıydı. Şimdi para biriktiriyor ve ofise uyanık ve keyifli varıyor. Tabii sorunlar da var. Yağmur yağınca ıslanıyor, kışın eve dönerken hava karanlık oluyor. Eşi yolların tehlikeli olduğunu düşünüyor, o yüzden Tolga hep kask ve parlak kıyafet giyiyor. Bir daha asla arabaya dönmeyeceğini söylüyor.

questions.q: How long is Tolga's journey to work?
questions.note: "The journey was only six kilometers."

questions.q: Why did the car journey take so long?
questions.note: "It often took him thirty minutes because of the traffic."

questions.q: What happened after two weeks?
options: He was faster than his car
questions.note: "After two weeks he was faster than his car."

questions.q: What does his wife think?
questions.note: "His wife thinks the roads are dangerous."

questions.q: What does Tolga wear?
questions.note: "Tolga always wears a helmet and bright clothes."

title: Kütüphanedeki sessizlik
text: Ece studies at the city library almost every afternoon. She likes it because it is quiet and she cannot look at her phone there. The rule is simple: no telephones, no food, no talking. Last week a group of students came in and started to talk about a film. The other readers looked at them, but nobody said anything. Finally an old man stood up and asked them politely to be quiet. The students apologized and moved to the cafe downstairs. Ece thought about this for a long time. She realized that she never says anything when something is wrong. Now she is trying to speak up more often.
textTr: Ece neredeyse her öğleden sonra şehir kütüphanesinde ders çalışıyor. Orayı seviyor çünkü sessiz ve orada telefonuna bakamıyor. Kural basit: telefon yok, yiyecek yok, konuşma yok. Geçen hafta bir grup öğrenci geldi ve bir film hakkında konuşmaya başladı. Diğer okuyucular onlara baktı ama kimse bir şey söylemedi. Sonunda yaşlı bir adam ayağa kalkıp kibarca sessiz olmalarını istedi. Öğrenciler özür dileyip alt kattaki kafeye gittiler. Ece bunu uzun süre düşündü. Bir şey yanlış olduğunda hiçbir zaman bir şey söylemediğini fark etti. Artık daha sık sesini çıkarmaya çalışıyor.

questions.q: Why does Ece like the library?
options: It is quiet and she cannot use her phone
questions.note: "She likes it because it is quiet and she cannot look at her phone there."

questions.q: What did the students do?
questions.note: "A group of students came in and started to talk about a film."

questions.q: Who spoke to the students?
questions.note: "An old man stood up and asked them politely to be quiet."

questions.q: What did the students do then?
questions.note: "The students apologized and moved to the cafe downstairs."

questions.q: What did Ece realize about herself?
questions.note: "She never says anything when something is wrong."

title: Balkonda bahçe
text: Fatma lives on the sixth floor and she has no garden. Two years ago her daughter gave her three small plants for her birthday. Fatma put them on the balcony and watered them every morning. They grew quickly, so she bought more. Now the balcony is full of green: tomatoes, peppers, mint and flowers of many colors. In summer she eats a salad from her own balcony almost every day. Her neighbor on the fifth floor started a small garden too, and they exchange plants. Fatma says the best part is not the food. It is that she has something to look after, and a reason to open the door every morning.
textTr: Fatma altıncı katta yaşıyor ve bahçesi yok. İki yıl önce kızı doğum gününde ona üç küçük bitki verdi. Fatma onları balkona koydu ve her sabah suladı. Hızla büyüdüler, o da daha fazla aldı. Şimdi balkon yemyeşil: domates, biber, nane ve birçok renkte çiçek. Yazın neredeyse her gün kendi balkonundan salata yiyor. Beşinci kattaki komşusu da küçük bir bahçe kurdu ve bitki değiş tokuşu yapıyorlar. Fatma en güzel kısmın yiyecek olmadığını söylüyor. Asıl güzel olan, bakacak bir şeyinin ve her sabah kapıyı açmak için bir sebebinin olması.

questions.q: Who gave Fatma the first plants?
questions.note: "Her daughter gave her three small plants for her birthday."

questions.q: What grows on the balcony now?
questions.note: "Tomatoes, peppers, mint and flowers of many colors."

questions.q: What does Fatma do with her neighbor?
questions.note: "They exchange plants."

questions.q: What does Fatma like most?
questions.note: En güzel kısım bakacak bir şeyinin olması.

questions.q: How often does she eat her own salad in summer?
questions.note: "In summer she eats a salad from her own balcony almost every day."

title: Pazar günü pazarı
text: Every Sunday morning a market opens in our street. The men arrive at six o'clock and build the stalls. By eight the street is full of people. You can buy vegetables, fruit, cheese, clothes and cheap kitchen things. My mother goes early because the best tomatoes are gone by ten. She always talks to the same man about the price, and they both enjoy it. Nothing really changes, but she says it is part of the shopping. I go with her to carry the heavy bags. Around one o'clock the men start to pack. By three the street is empty and clean again, and only a few boxes show that the market was there at all.
textTr: Her pazar sabahı sokağımızda bir pazar kuruluyor. Adamlar altıda gelip tezgâhları kuruyor. Sekizde sokak insanla doluyor. Sebze, meyve, peynir, kıyafet ve ucuz mutfak eşyası alabilirsin. Annem erken gidiyor çünkü en iyi domatesler ona kadar bitiyor. Hep aynı adamla fiyat konusunda konuşuyor ve ikisi de bundan keyif alıyor. Aslında bir şey değişmiyor ama annem bunun alışverişin parçası olduğunu söylüyor. Ağır poşetleri taşımak için onunla gidiyorum. Saat bire doğru adamlar toplamaya başlıyor. Üçte sokak yeniden boş ve temiz oluyor; pazarın orada olduğunu sadece birkaç kutu gösteriyor.

questions.q: What time do the men arrive?
questions.note: "The men arrive at six o'clock."

questions.q: Why does the mother go early?
options: The best tomatoes are gone by ten
questions.note: "The best tomatoes are gone by ten."

questions.q: What does the mother do with the same man?
questions.note: "She always talks to the same man about the price."

questions.q: Why does the writer go with her?
questions.note: "I go with her to carry the heavy bags."

questions.q: What is the street like at three?
questions.note: "By three the street is empty and clean again."

title: Ehliyet sınavı
text: I took my driving test three times. The first time I was so nervous that I forgot to look in the mirror. The examiner stopped the test after ten minutes. The second time I drove well for twenty minutes, but then I stopped in the wrong place and a bus had to wait. My teacher Murat told me the problem was not my driving. He said I was thinking about the test instead of the road. Before the third test he made me drive for an hour without saying anything about the exam. That morning I was calmer. I passed. Now I drive to work every day and I still remember that advice when the traffic is bad.
textTr: Ehliyet sınavına üç kez girdim. İlk seferde o kadar gergindim ki aynaya bakmayı unuttum. Sınav görevlisi on dakika sonra sınavı bitirdi. İkinci seferde yirmi dakika iyi sürdüm ama sonra yanlış yerde durdum ve bir otobüs beklemek zorunda kaldı. Hocam Murat sorunun sürüşüm olmadığını söyledi. Yolu değil sınavı düşündüğümü söyledi. Üçüncü sınavdan önce bana bir saat boyunca sınavdan hiç bahsetmeden araba sürdürdü. O sabah daha sakindim. Geçtim. Şimdi her gün işe arabayla gidiyorum ve trafik kötü olduğunda hâlâ o tavsiyeyi hatırlıyorum.

questions.q: What went wrong the first time?
options: He forgot to look in the mirror
He stopped in the wrong place
questions.note: "I forgot to look in the mirror."

questions.q: What happened the second time?
options: He stopped in the wrong place
questions.note: "I stopped in the wrong place and a bus had to wait."

questions.q: What did Murat say the real problem was?
options: He was thinking about the test
questions.note: "He said I was thinking about the test instead of the road."

questions.q: What did Murat do before the third test?
options: Made him drive without talking about the exam
questions.note: "He made me drive for an hour without saying anything about the exam."

questions.q: What does the writer remember now?
questions.note: "I still remember that advice when the traffic is bad."

title: Yeni bir dil öğrenmek
text: My aunt Ayla started to learn German when she was forty-five. Everybody in the family said she was too old. She went to a class two evenings a week after work. In the first year she could only say simple sentences and she often felt stupid next to the young students. She did not stop. She wrote new words on small papers and put them on the kitchen door. After three years she went to Berlin alone for a week. She told me it was the best week of her life because she could ask questions and understand the answers. She is fifty now and she is learning her third language.
textTr: Teyzem Ayla kırk beş yaşında Almanca öğrenmeye başladı. Ailede herkes onun çok yaşlı olduğunu söyledi. İşten sonra haftada iki akşam kursa gitti. İlk yıl sadece basit cümleler kurabiliyordu ve genç öğrencilerin yanında sık sık kendini aptal gibi hissediyordu. Bırakmadı. Yeni kelimeleri küçük kâğıtlara yazıp mutfak kapısına astı. Üç yıl sonra bir haftalığına tek başına Berlin'e gitti. Bana hayatının en güzel haftası olduğunu söyledi çünkü soru sorabiliyor ve cevapları anlayabiliyordu. Şimdi elli yaşında ve üçüncü dilini öğreniyor.

questions.q: How old was Ayla when she started?
questions.note: "She started to learn German when she was forty-five."

questions.q: What did the family say?
questions.note: "Everybody in the family said she was too old."

questions.q: How did she feel in the first year?
options: Stupid next to the young students
questions.note: "She often felt stupid next to the young students."

questions.q: Where did she put the new words?
questions.note: "She wrote new words on small papers and put them on the kitchen door."

questions.q: Why was the week in Berlin the best?
options: She could ask questions and understand
questions.note: "Because she could ask questions and understand the answers."

title: Kardeşimle paylaştığım oda
text: I shared a room with my brother Efe for eleven years. We are very different. I go to bed early and I need a quiet room. He works until two in the morning and he listens to music while he works. For a long time we argued almost every night. Then my father drew a line on the floor with tape. It was a joke, but it helped. We made three rules: no music after midnight, no clothes on the other side of the line, and nobody touches the other one's desk. The rules worked better than the arguments. Last month Efe moved to another city for university. The room is quiet now and I do not like it as much as I expected.
textTr: Kardeşim Efe ile on bir yıl aynı odayı paylaştım. Çok farklıyız. Ben erken yatıyorum ve sessiz bir oda istiyorum. O sabah ikiye kadar çalışıyor ve çalışırken müzik dinliyor. Uzun süre neredeyse her gece tartıştık. Sonra babam bantla yere bir çizgi çekti. Şakaydı ama işe yaradı. Üç kural koyduk: gece yarısından sonra müzik yok, çizginin öbür tarafında kıyafet yok ve kimse diğerinin masasına dokunmuyor. Kurallar tartışmalardan daha iyi işledi. Geçen ay Efe üniversite için başka bir şehre taşındı. Oda şimdi sessiz ve bunu beklediğim kadar sevmedim.

questions.q: How long did they share the room?
questions.note: "I shared a room with my brother Efe for eleven years."

questions.q: What is the difference between them?
options: One sleeps early, one works late
questions.note: "I go to bed early... He works until two in the morning."

questions.q: How did the father end the arguments?
options: He drew a line on the floor
questions.note: "My father drew a line on the floor with tape."

questions.q: How many rules did they make?
questions.note: "We made three rules."

questions.q: How does the writer feel now?
options: He likes the quiet less than he expected
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Kırık saat
text: My grandfather gave me his watch before he died. It stopped working two years later. I took it to three shops. The first two said it was too old and the parts do not exist any more. The third shop was very small and dark, behind the fish market. The man there, Sabri, looked at it for a long time without saying anything. Then he said he could not buy the parts but he could make one. It took him a month and it was not cheap. My friends say I paid too much for an old watch that is not worth the money. They are right about the money. But when I wear it I can hear it, and that is what I paid for.
textTr: Dedem ölmeden önce bana saatini verdi. İki yıl sonra durdu. Üç dükkâna götürdüm. İlk ikisi çok eski olduğunu ve parçalarının artık bulunmadığını söyledi. Üçüncü dükkân çok küçük ve karanlıktı, balık pazarının arkasındaydı. Oradaki adam, Sabri, hiçbir şey söylemeden saate uzun süre baktı. Sonra parçayı satın alamayacağını ama yapabileceğini söyledi. Bir ayını aldı ve ucuz değildi. Arkadaşlarım paranın etmediği eski bir saate çok para verdiğimi söylüyor. Para konusunda haklılar. Ama onu taktığımda sesini duyabiliyorum ve parayı bunun için verdim.

questions.q: Who gave the writer the watch?
questions.note: "My grandfather gave me his watch."

questions.q: What did the first two shops say?
options: The parts do not exist any more
It was too expensive to fix
questions.note: "It was too old and the parts do not exist any more."

questions.q: Where was the third shop?
questions.note: "Behind the fish market."

questions.q: What did Sabri do?
questions.note: "He could not buy the parts but he could make one."

questions.q: What does the writer say about the money?
options: His friends are right, but he does not mind
questions.note: "They are right about the money."

title: İlk maaş
text: My cousin Onur got his first salary last month. He is nineteen and he works in a shop at the weekend. On Monday he came to our house with a big bag. He bought a present for his mother, a shirt for his father and chocolate for everybody. By Wednesday he had almost no money left. My mother said nothing at the time. Two weeks later she asked him quietly how the month was going. He said it was difficult. She did not tell him he was stupid. She only said that her first salary went the same way. Next month he wants to save half of it. I do not know if he will, but he has a plan now.
textTr: Kuzenim Onur geçen ay ilk maaşını aldı. On dokuz yaşında ve hafta sonları bir dükkânda çalışıyor. Pazartesi elinde büyük bir poşetle evimize geldi. Annesine hediye, babasına gömlek ve herkese çikolata almış. Çarşambaya kadar neredeyse hiç parası kalmamıştı. Annem o an bir şey söylemedi. İki hafta sonra ona sessizce ayın nasıl gittiğini sordu. Zor olduğunu söyledi. Annem ona aptal olduğunu söylemedi. Sadece kendi ilk maaşının da aynı şekilde gittiğini söyledi. Gelecek ay yarısını biriktirmek istiyor. Yapar mı bilmiyorum ama artık bir planı var.

questions.q: Where does Onur work?
options: In a shop at the weekend
questions.note: "He works in a shop at the weekend."

questions.q: What did he buy for his father?
questions.note: "A shirt for his father."

questions.q: When did the money run out?
questions.note: "By Wednesday he had almost no money left."

questions.q: What did the mother say two weeks later?
options: He must give the money back
Her first salary went the same way
questions.note: "She only said that her first salary went the same way."

questions.q: What does Onur want to do next month?
questions.note: "Next month he wants to save half of it."

title: Sınav gecesi
text: The night before an important exam I usually cannot sleep. Last June I had a history exam at nine in the morning. At midnight I was still reading my notes. At one o'clock I decided to sleep, but my head was full of dates. At three I got up and made tea. My sister Pinar found me in the kitchen. She is a nurse and she works at night, so she was awake too. She told me to stop reading and to talk about something else. We talked about her work for half an hour. Then I slept until seven. In the exam I remembered everything. Now I always stop reading at eleven.
textTr: Önemli bir sınavdan önceki gece genelde uyuyamam. Geçen haziran sabah dokuzda tarih sınavım vardı. Gece yarısı hâlâ notlarımı okuyordum. Birde uyumaya karar verdim ama kafam tarihlerle doluydu. Üçte kalkıp çay yaptım. Kız kardeşim Pınar beni mutfakta buldu. Hemşire ve geceleri çalışıyor, o yüzden o da uyanıktı. Bana okumayı bırakıp başka bir şeyden konuşmamı söyledi. Yarım saat onun işini konuştuk. Sonra yediye kadar uyudum. Sınavda her şeyi hatırladım. Artık hep on birde okumayı bırakıyorum.

questions.q: What time was the exam?
questions.note: "I had a history exam at nine in the morning."

questions.q: Why was Pinar awake?
questions.note: "She is a nurse and she works at night."

questions.q: What did Pinar tell her to do?
options: Stop reading and talk about something else
questions.note: "She told me to stop reading and to talk about something else."

questions.q: How long did they talk?
questions.note: "We talked about her work for half an hour."

questions.q: What does the writer do now?
questions.note: "Now I always stop reading at eleven."

title: Balkondan gelen ses
text: For two weeks we heard a strange noise from the balcony at night. My mother thought it was a bird. My father thought it was the wind. I thought somebody was there and I did not sleep well. On Saturday morning we looked properly. Behind the old chairs there was a small box, and inside the box there were four young cats. Our neighbor Sema said the mother cat comes every night through the open window. We wanted to keep them but my father said no. Sema found homes for three of them. The fourth one still lives with us. My father feeds her every morning and he says he is only doing it because nobody else will.
textTr: İki hafta boyunca geceleri balkondan tuhaf bir ses duyduk. Annem kuş olduğunu düşündü. Babam rüzgâr olduğunu düşündü. Ben orada biri olduğunu düşündüm ve iyi uyuyamadım. Cumartesi sabahı düzgünce baktık. Eski sandalyelerin arkasında küçük bir kutu vardı ve kutunun içinde dört yavru kedi vardı. Komşumuz Sema anne kedinin her gece açık pencereden geldiğini söyledi. Onları tutmak istedik ama babam hayır dedi. Sema üçüne yuva buldu. Dördüncüsü hâlâ bizimle yaşıyor. Babam her sabah onu besliyor ve bunu sadece başka kimse yapmayacağı için yaptığını söylüyor.

questions.q: How long did they hear the noise?
questions.note: "For two weeks we heard a strange noise."

questions.q: What did the father think it was?
questions.note: "My father thought it was the wind."

questions.q: What did they find in the box?
questions.note: "Inside the box there were four young cats."

questions.q: Who found homes for the cats?
questions.note: "Sema found homes for three of them."

questions.q: What does the father do now?
questions.note: "My father feeds her every morning."

title: Fotoğraf makinesi
text: My friend Tolga bought an old camera at a second-hand shop. It uses film, so you cannot see the photo after you take it. You must wait and pay to see the pictures. At first I thought this was stupid. Why pay for something when your phone is free? Then he showed me his first photos. Only twenty of the thirty-six were good, but he could talk about every one of them. He remembered where he stood and why he took it. I take two hundred photos on a holiday and I do not remember any of them. Last week I asked him where the shop was.
textTr: Arkadaşım Tolga ikinci el bir dükkândan eski bir fotoğraf makinesi aldı. Film kullanıyor, yani çektikten sonra fotoğrafı göremiyorsun. Beklemen ve resimleri görmek için para ödemen gerekiyor. Başta bunun aptalca olduğunu düşündüm. Telefonun bedavayken neden para ödeyesin? Sonra bana ilk fotoğraflarını gösterdi. Otuz altının sadece yirmisi iyiydi ama her biri hakkında konuşabiliyordu. Nerede durduğunu ve neden çektiğini hatırlıyordu. Ben bir tatilde iki yüz fotoğraf çekiyorum ve hiçbirini hatırlamıyorum. Geçen hafta ona dükkânın nerede olduğunu sordum.

questions.q: What is special about the camera?
questions.note: "It uses film."

questions.q: What did the writer think at first?
questions.note: "At first I thought this was stupid."

questions.q: How many photos were good?
questions.note: "Only twenty of the thirty-six were good."

questions.q: What could Tolga do with every photo?
questions.note: "He could talk about every one of them."

questions.q: What did the writer do last week?
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Yanlış anlaşılan şaka
text: At work last month I made a joke about my colleague Berk. Everybody laughed, and I thought he laughed too. The next day he was very quiet. He did not come to lunch with us. I thought he was busy. On Friday another colleague told me that Berk was upset about the joke. I felt terrible. I did not want to write a message because it is easy to write the wrong thing. So on Monday I asked him for a coffee and I said sorry. He said the joke was not really the problem; the problem was that it was in front of ten people. He was right. Now I am more careful about where I say things.
textTr: Geçen ay işte meslektaşım Berk hakkında bir şaka yaptım. Herkes güldü ve onun da güldüğünü sandım. Ertesi gün çok sessizdi. Bizimle öğle yemeğine gelmedi. Meşgul sandım. Cuma günü başka bir meslektaşım Berk'in şakaya üzüldüğünü söyledi. Berbat hissettim. Mesaj yazmak istemedim çünkü yanlış bir şey yazmak kolay. O yüzden pazartesi ona kahve teklif ettim ve özür diledim. Asıl sorunun şaka olmadığını, on kişinin önünde olması olduğunu söyledi. Haklıydı. Artık bir şeyi nerede söylediğime daha çok dikkat ediyorum.

questions.q: How did the writer read the room?
questions.note: "I thought he laughed too."

questions.q: How did the writer find out?
questions.note: "On Friday another colleague told me."

questions.q: Why did the writer not send a message?
options: It is easy to write the wrong thing
questions.note: "Because it is easy to write the wrong thing."

questions.q: What did Berk say the real problem was?
options: It was said in front of ten people
questions.note: "The problem was that it was in front of ten people."

questions.q: What is the writer more careful about now?
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Yağmurda kalan düğün
text: My cousin Gizem planned her wedding in a garden. She checked the weather every day for a month. On the morning of the wedding the sky was blue. At six in the evening, ten minutes before the start, it began to rain. Everybody ran inside the small house. There were a hundred guests and not enough chairs. People sat on the stairs and on the kitchen table. The music did not work. Gizem cried for five minutes and then she laughed. Her photos are the funniest photos I have ever seen. She says now that a perfect garden wedding would have been forgotten in a year.
textTr: Kuzenim Gizem düğününü bir bahçede planladı. Bir ay boyunca her gün havayı kontrol etti. Düğün sabahı gökyüzü maviydi. Akşam altıda, başlamadan on dakika önce yağmur başladı. Herkes küçük evin içine koştu. Yüz misafir vardı ve yeterince sandalye yoktu. İnsanlar merdivenlere ve mutfak masasına oturdu. Müzik çalışmadı. Gizem beş dakika ağladı, sonra güldü. Fotoğrafları gördüğüm en komik fotoğraflar. Şimdi kusursuz bir bahçe düğününün bir yılda unutulacağını söylüyor.

questions.q: Where was the wedding planned?
questions.note: "Gizem planned her wedding in a garden."

questions.q: When did it start to rain?
questions.note: "At six in the evening, ten minutes before the start, it began to rain."

questions.q: What was the problem inside?
questions.note: "There were a hundred guests and not enough chairs."

questions.q: What did Gizem do?
questions.note: "Gizem cried for five minutes and then she laughed."

questions.q: What does she say now?
options: A perfect wedding would have been forgotten
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Koşmaya başlamak
text: In January I decided to start running. On the first day I ran for four minutes and then I had to walk. I was very tired and my legs hurt for two days. A friend told me the mistake was clear: I started too fast. She said to run slowly enough to talk at the same time. It felt silly, but I tried it. After six weeks I could run for twenty minutes without stopping. I am still slow. Cars, bicycles and even some people who are walking fast pass me. But in January I could not run for five minutes, and now I run three times a week.
textTr: Ocakta koşmaya başlamaya karar verdim. İlk gün dört dakika koştum, sonra yürümek zorunda kaldım. Çok yorgundum ve bacaklarım iki gün ağrıdı. Bir arkadaşım hatanın belli olduğunu söyledi: çok hızlı başlamışım. Aynı anda konuşabilecek kadar yavaş koşmamı söyledi. Saçma geldi ama denedim. Altı hafta sonra durmadan yirmi dakika koşabiliyordum. Hâlâ yavaşım. Arabalar, bisikletler, hatta hızlı yürüyen bazı insanlar beni geçiyor. Ama ocakta beş dakika koşamıyordum, şimdi haftada üç kez koşuyorum.

questions.q: How long did the writer run on the first day?
questions.note: "On the first day I ran for four minutes."

questions.q: What was the mistake?
questions.note: "I started too fast."

questions.q: What was the friend's advice?
questions.note: "She said to run slowly enough to talk at the same time."

questions.q: What could the writer do after six weeks?
questions.note: "After six weeks I could run for twenty minutes without stopping."

questions.q: How often does the writer run now?
questions.note: "Now I run three times a week."

title: Dedemin defterleri
text: When we cleaned my grandfather's house we found twenty-two notebooks under his bed. He wrote in one every year from 1968. They are not about big things. He wrote what the weather was, what he paid for bread, who came to visit and what they said. On the first page of 1971 he wrote only four words: today my son arrived. That son is my father. My father read that page three times and then he closed the book. We put the notebooks in a box in our living room. My mother wants to type them on the computer. I think she is right, but nobody has started yet.
textTr: Dedemin evini temizlerken yatağının altında yirmi iki defter bulduk. 1968'den itibaren her yıl birine yazmış. Büyük şeylerle ilgili değiller. Havanın nasıl olduğunu, ekmeğe ne verdiğini, kimin ziyarete geldiğini ve ne söylediğini yazmış. 1971'in ilk sayfasına sadece dört kelime yazmış: bugün oğlum geldi. O oğul benim babam. Babam o sayfayı üç kez okudu ve sonra defteri kapattı. Defterleri oturma odamızdaki bir kutuya koyduk. Annem onları bilgisayara geçirmek istiyor. Bence haklı ama henüz kimse başlamadı.

questions.q: Where were the notebooks?
questions.note: "We found twenty-two notebooks under his bed."

questions.q: What did the grandfather write about?
questions.note: "He wrote what the weather was, what he paid for bread."

questions.q: What did he write in 1971?
questions.note: "Today my son arrived."

questions.q: How did the father react?
options: He read the page three times
He put the book away at once
questions.note: "My father read that page three times."

questions.q: What does the mother want to do?
questions.note: "My mother wants to type them on the computer."

title: Ev arkadaşı ilanı
text: When my flatmate moved out I put a small advertisement on the internet. Twelve people wrote to me in three days. I met six of them in a cafe near the flat. One man asked only about the price. One woman asked if she could bring two dogs. Another person did not come and did not write. Then Cansu came. She asked what time I get up, if I cook, and if I mind people in the kitchen late at night. Those were the right questions. She has lived here for eight months now and we have never argued about anything important.
textTr: Ev arkadaşım taşınınca internete küçük bir ilan koydum. Üç günde on iki kişi bana yazdı. Altısıyla evin yakınındaki bir kafede buluştum. Bir adam sadece fiyatı sordu. Bir kadın iki köpek getirip getiremeyeceğini sordu. Başka biri ne geldi ne de yazdı. Sonra Cansu geldi. Saat kaçta kalktığımı, yemek yapıp yapmadığımı ve gece geç saatte mutfakta insan olmasından rahatsız olup olmadığımı sordu. Doğru sorular bunlardı. Sekiz aydır burada yaşıyor ve önemli hiçbir şey için tartışmadık.

questions.q: How many people wrote in three days?
questions.note: "Twelve people wrote to me in three days."

questions.q: What did one man ask about?
questions.note: "One man asked only about the price."

questions.q: What did Cansu ask about?
questions.note: "She asked what time I get up, if I cook."

questions.q: How long has Cansu lived there?
questions.note: "She has lived here for eight months now."

questions.q: What does the writer say about them?
options: They have never argued about anything important
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Gece treni
text: Last winter I went to Adana by bus. The journey was twelve hours and it started at nine in the evening. I had a seat near the window. Next to me sat an old woman with a large bag of food. After one hour she opened the bag and gave me bread and cheese. I said no twice and then I said yes. She talked about her four children for three hours. I was tired and I wanted to sleep, but her stories were better than sleeping. At six in the morning her son met her at the station. She gave me the rest of the bread and she did not ask for my name.
textTr: Geçen kış Adana'ya otobüsle gittim. Yolculuk on iki saatti ve akşam dokuzda başladı. Pencere kenarında oturdum. Yanımda büyük bir yiyecek çantası olan yaşlı bir kadın oturuyordu. Bir saat sonra çantayı açtı ve bana ekmek ve peynir verdi. İki kez hayır dedim, sonra evet dedim. Üç saat boyunca dört çocuğundan bahsetti. Yorgundum ve uyumak istiyordum ama hikâyeleri uykudan iyiydi. Sabah altıda oğlu onu garda karşıladı. Kalan ekmeği bana verdi ve adımı sormadı.

questions.q: How long was the journey?
questions.note: "The journey was twelve hours."

questions.q: What did the old woman have?
questions.note: "An old woman with a large bag of food."

questions.q: How did the writer answer at first?
questions.note: "I said no twice and then I said yes."

questions.q: Why did the writer not sleep?
options: Her stories were better than sleeping
questions.note: "Her stories were better than sleeping."

questions.q: What did she do at the end?
options: Gave him the rest of the bread
questions.note: Son cümle.
